sentences.text:
Instant criminal appeal has been filed by the appellants under Section 374(2) Cr.P.C. against the judgment dated 30.07.2003 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge,
Sangaria, in Sessions Case No.8/2002 (Old No.9/2002) by which the learned Judge convicted and sentenced the appellants as under :
S.No. Offence U/s Sentence Fine Sentence in default of fine 1. 306 IPC 7 years' RI Rs.1,000/- 3 months' SI 2. 498A IPC 3 years' RI Rs.500/- 2 months' SI Both the sentences were ordered to run concurrently.

Brief facts of the case are that on 08.10.2001 at about 1:30 PM, ASI Jaipal of PS Sangaria recorded the statement of injured [2024:RJ-JD:12122] (2 of 4) [CRLA-826/2003] Vinod Devi at Govt.
Hospital Sangaria, where she was admitted due to severe burn injuries.

In her statement, Vinod Devi stated that her marriage was solemnized with appellant No.1 Surya Prakash about six years ago Surya Prakash And Anr vs State (2024:Rj-Jd:12122) on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29147093/
1 and at the time of marriage, her father gave sufficient dowry.

entities.text: Surya Prakash And Anr vs State (2024:Rj-Jd:12122)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But, after some time of marriage, her husband and in-laws started harassing her mentally and physically for bringing less dowry.

Today,
when she was alone at home, she poured kerosene oil on herself and lit the fire.
Later on, Vinod Devi died due to severe burn injuries.
On the basis of the aforesaid statement, the Police registered a case and started investigation.
On completion of investigation, police filed challan against the accused-appellants and co-accused Rajbala.
Thereafter, the charges for offence under Sections 304B, 406, 498A IPC were framed by the trial court against the accused-appellants and co- accused, who pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
During the course of trial, the prosecution examined as many as 22 witnesses in support of its case and also exhibited some documents.
Thereafter, statements of the accused appellants and co-accused were recorded under section 313 Cr.P.C.
Upon conclusion of the trial, the learned trial court vide impugned judgment dated 30.07.2003 convicted and sentenced the accused-appellants for the offences as aforesaid.
Hence, this criminal appeal.

At the threshold, learned counsel for the accused-appellants submits that he does not challenge the finding of conviction but since the occurrence is related to the year 2001, and the father of the deceased and other witnesses have been declared hostile, and [2024:RJ-JD:12122] (3 of 4)
[CRLA-826/2003] the appellant No.1 has so far suffered a sentence of about one year & six months and appellant No.2 has suffered a sentence of eight & half months, out of total sentence of seven years' R.I., therefore, it is prayed that the sentence awarded to the appellants for the aforesaid offences may be reduced to the period already undergone by them.
Learned Public Prosecutor opposed the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellants.
The learned PP submitted that there is neither any occasion to interfere with the sentence awarded to the accused appellants nor any compassion or sympathy is called for in the said case.
I have perused the evidence of the prosecution as well as defence and the judgment passed by the trial court regarding conviction of the accused-appellants.
Undisputedly, the occurrence relates back to year 2001 and the appellant No.1 has so far undergone a period of about one year & six months incarceration and appellant No.2 has so far undergone a period of about eight & half months incarceration, out of total sentence of seven years' R.I., and has also suffered the mental agony and trauma of protracted trial.

Thus, looking to the over-all circumstances and the facts that the father of the deceased and other witnesses have been declared hostile by the trial court and the appellants have remained behind the bars for a considerable period, it will be just and proper if the sentence awarded by the trial court for offence under Sections 306, 498A IPC is reduced to the period already undergone by the appellants.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed.

While maintaining the appellants' conviction and sentence for offence under Sections [2024:RJ-JD:12122] (4 of 4) [CRLA-826/2003] 306, 498A IPC, the sentence awarded to them for the said offences is hereby reduced to the period already undergone.
The fine imposed by the trial court is hereby maintained.
Three months' time is granted to deposit the fine before the trial court.
In default of payment of fine, the appellants shall undergo one month's simple imprisonment.
The fine amount, if any, already deposited by the appellants shall be adjusted.
The appellants are on bail.
They need not surrender.
their bail bonds are discharged.
Record, if received, be sent back forthwith.

(MANOJ KUMAR GARG),J 219-MS/-
